assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small-molecule recognition into a new therapeutic modality: a bifunctional or glue-like molecule recruits an E3 ligase and removes a protein rather than inhibiting it. It opens previously undruggable targets and is a clear case of chemical design principles changing what researchers and clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Crews conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept (with Deshaies and Sakamoto in the first report) and developed it into drugs; Ciulli made the VHL ligands and degrader design principles; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underpins the glue-degrader branch. Credit across the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands is split, so a three-person prize is a compromise.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials, with confirmation across labs, companies and E3 ligases. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is still pending, but the chemistry and mechanism are firmly established, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one prize or whether the concept (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) outranks the CRBN glue mechanism (Handa, Ito).
Deshaies and Sakamoto are omitted from a three-person slate; I cannot independently verify the relative priority of their 2001 contribution.
No PROTAC has yet been approved, so clinical impact is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation makes proteins by chemistry: unprotected peptide segments join chemoselectively at a cysteine to form a native peptide bond. It enabled total chemical synthesis, semisynthesis, site-specific labeling and modified proteins, with broad use across chemical biology and biomaterials.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson developed and introduced the ligation (with Muir and Dawson in the original 1994 work); Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu contributed important later methods. A Kent, Muir, Dawson group is defensible but leaves out meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent use and clear impact in protein science. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Weight between the original ligation (Kent, Dawson) and the semisynthesis extension (Muir).
Contributions of Danishefsky, Brik and Liu may be judged equal to the proposed subset.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs let cells incorporate genetically encoded noncanonical amino acids, giving chemists atomic-level control over proteins in living systems. It has been used for bioorthogonal handles, crosslinkers, photocaging and therapeutic proteins, and for engineering new materials from designed proteins.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial orthogonal pairs and the general strategy; Chin extended it to multiple codons, quadruplet decoding and whole-genome recoding. Yokoyama and Mehl also contributed pairs and structural work. A three-person split is plausible but requires judgment.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and applied over two decades, including in industry. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Selection among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Yokoyama and Mehl is not obvious.
I am relying on my background knowledge for the exact priority of the early orthogonal pair demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without double-strand breaks, a molecular-design solution that gives precise genome editing. Its clinical relevance is already visible, and the approach exemplifies chemistry at the interface of engineering and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual design and development of both cytosine and adenine base editors, and the single-name award is clean; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on the key papers. Nishida and Kondo made an independent related cytidine-deaminase fusion. Naming Liu alone is the clearest configuration but may undercredit co-first authors.
assessment.maturity: Strong reproducibility and first clinical results, but the field is still maturing and the 2020 CRISPR prize adjacent to this area may raise a bar for overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prior CRISPR-Cas9 chemistry prize may affect how the committee views novelty.
Whether prime editing (B024) should be combined with base editing in one Liu recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery technology that made siRNA and mRNA medicines possible, including the COVID-19 vaccines. This is a case where molecular design of lipid chemistry, self-assembly and pKa tuning directly changed clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led foundational work on lipid nanoparticle formation and ionizable lipids with collaborators such as Hope and Madden; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid discovery and optimization. Attribution is diffuse and industrial contributions are hard to separate, so any three-person subset is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Impact is demonstrated at the scale of billions of doses. The mRNA vaccine recognition in Medicine (2023) may make a Chemistry prize here seem partially redundant.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.
Credit division among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is uncertain and in part dependent on patents and company work I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids give programmable, Watson-Crick-governed control of nanoparticle organization and surfaces, with applications in biosensing and diagnostics, intracellular gene regulation, and crystal engineering. It sits close to my own area of peptide- and nanoparticle-based biosensors.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently introduced DNA-nanoparticle conjugates and assembly in 1996, and Mirkin developed spherical nucleic acids and colorimetric detection. Storhoff and Mucic are credited trainees. A Mirkin-Alivisatos pairing is a natural, though Alivisatos is better known for nanocrystal synthesis.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the lab and widely used, with some clinical and commercial products, but translational impact is more modest than for degraders or LNPs.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would credit Alivisatos for this work rather than for nanocrystal quantum dots.
Real-world clinical impact beyond diagnostics is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to report on the functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes, enabling target and inhibitor discovery directly in native biology. It turned chemical reactivity into a general proteomic readout and is now used in drug discovery and in covalent ligand screening.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt established ABPP as a general proteomic platform; Bogyo and Overkleeft developed probes for proteases and proteasome and for imaging. Weerapana contributed reactive-cysteine profiling. A Cravatt-led group with Bogyo and Overkleeft is reasonable, though Cravatt alone is also arguable.
assessment.maturity: Well established with extensive independent use and clinical-stage compounds from its screens. Timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be Cravatt alone or a larger group.
Its practical connection to approved drugs is indirect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically, culminating in portable nanopore DNA and RNA sequencing. Engineered protein pores and the single-molecule detection concepts are a strong example of molecular engineering feeding analytical tools used by clinicians and in the field.
assessment.attribution: Branton, Deamer and collaborators proposed and demonstrated DNA translocation through pores, Kasianowicz showed single-molecule detection, Bayley engineered protein pores for sensing, and Akeson demonstrated strand-level control. Attribution is complicated, and Oxford Nanopore commercial development involved many others.
assessment.maturity: Mature technology with broad adoption, though the sequencing application is closer to biology and genomics prizes.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson.
Possible view that sequencing impact belongs outside the scope of Chemistry.
